title: Kenyan Coffee Cake
community: Urban Kenya — celebrating Kenya's world-class coffee
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Coffee Cake — a deeply flavoured coffee sponge made with Kenya AA or Nyeri single-origin coffee, layered with coffee buttercream and dusted with cocoa. A celebration of Kenya's world-class coffee in cake form — the café dessert that makes visitors understand why Kenyan coffee is legendary.
longDesc: Kenya produces some of the world's finest coffee — the volcanic soils of Nyeri, Kirinyaga, and the slopes of Mount Kenya yield beans with extraordinary brightness, fruit complexity, and depth. Using strong brewed Kenyan coffee in a cake amplifies these qualities — the result is a coffee cake with more character than any other.
ingredients: 4 tbsp strong brewed Kenyan coffee — cooled
2 tsp coffee extract or additional 2 tbsp espresso
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and line tins.
Beat butter and sugar until pale and fluffy — 5 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time. Beat well.
Alternate adding flour and coffee-milk mixture in three additions.
Make buttercream: beat butter until pale. Add icing sugar, coffee, and vanilla. Beat until fluffy.
Fill and frost with coffee buttercream.
chefTips: Use the strongest, most flavourful Kenyan coffee you can find — Nyeri AA or Kirinyaga are ideal.
Cool the coffee completely before adding to the batter — warm coffee melts the butter.
The coffee buttercream is the star — be generous.
commonMistakes: Warm coffee in the batter — curdled mixture.
Under-beating the buttercream — not fluffy enough.
cookingScience: Coffee's aromatic compounds (furans, pyrazines, aldehydes) are released during brewing and partially survive baking. The fat in the butter carries these aromatic compounds into the cake crumb — the same reason coffee flavour is more intense in coffee ice cream (fat medium) than in coffee jelly.
sustainabilityTips: Use direct-trade Kenyan coffee — ensuring farmers receive fair prices for exceptional beans.
storage: Room temperature 3 days. Refrigerate up to 5 days.
culturalNote: Kenyan coffee cake is a statement of pride — Kenya produces some of the world's most sought-after coffee, and using it in a cake is the café's way of saying: we know what we have, and we celebrate it.
